# BUA Børne- og ungdomspsykiatri - Sengeafsnit

BUA Børne- og ungdomspsykiatri - Sengeafsnit is an inpatient ("sengeafsnit," i.e. bed/ward) unit of the child and adolescent psychiatry service under [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] [^src1] [^src3]. It appears repeatedly as a reporting unit in the Danish **ADHD-databasen**, the national quality-monitoring register for ADHD diagnosis and treatment pathways, to which it submits performance data on several quality indicators [^src8].

The unit's most notable documented result is a **100% fulfillment rate on Indikator 4** (95% CI: 3–100) in the ADHD-databasen's 2023 report, measuring coordinating network meetings held within 90 days of treatment start. BUA Børne- og ungdomspsykiatri - Sengeafsnit havde 100 % opfyldelse af indikator 4 (95% CI: 3-100) [^src1]. This figure, drawn from a small underlying case count, recurs in the 2023 report's later pages as well [^src2]. Indikator 4 is part of a broader set of quality measures that, nationally, showed dramatically low fulfillment against a 90% development target — the national average for this indicator was just 0% at the time, making the unit's reported 100% (albeit on a very wide confidence interval reflecting a small sample) a notable outlier [^src1] [^src2].

By the 2024 reporting cycle, however, the picture for this same unit becomes more mixed and, in places, harder to reconcile: pages from ADHD_2024.pdf show the unit at **25% (range 1–81)** on one measure [^src4] [^src5], at **0% (range 0–98)** on another [^src6] [^src7], and again at **100% (range 3–100)** on a further measure [^src8] — the latter matching the earlier 2023 result. The variation across these entries reflects the fact that the ADHD-databasen tracks multiple distinct indicators (diagnostic conferences within 120 days, coordinating network meetings within 90 days, psychoeducation within 120 days, and others), several of which were reported for this unit across different pages of the same document. Read together with the broader chunk context, this is consistent with a system-wide pattern: Danish child and adolescent psychiatry services in this period were operating under significant pressure, with long waiting times leading many units — including this one — to deprioritize treatment-adjacent tasks like coordinating network meetings and psychoeducation in favor of diagnostic assessment [^src8].

As an administrative matter, the unit is explicitly identified as a department under Region Midtjylland [^src1] and as an inpatient unit located within the Central Denmark Region [^src3], and it reports its results into the ADHD-databasen [^src8], the same database whose steering group has, according to the surrounding documentation, been revising several indicators (including the network-meeting indicator) in response to persistently low national performance.
